title: Why is the sky blue — and not violet?
summary: Air molecules scatter short-wavelength light far more than long-wavelength light. Blue wins over violet because sunlight has less violet and our eyes are less sensitive to it.

scenes.text: Sunlight is white. So why is the sky blue?
Sunlight contains every color. As it passes through air, tiny gas molecules scatter some of it in all directions.
Blue light (around 450 nm) is scattered about six times more strongly than red light (around 700 nm).
Violet scatters even more. So why isn't the sky violet?
scenes.answer: Sunlight contains less violet, some is absorbed high up, and our eyes are less sensitive to it.

scenes.text: At sunset, light passes through much more air to reach you.
scenes.reveal: Most of the blue is scattered away first, leaving reds and oranges.

scenes.text: A blue sky is sunlight bouncing off the air itself.
